tx-tarrant-2026-coa2-p2-taylor-chris.name: Chris Taylor
tx-tarrant-2026-coa2-p2-taylor-chris.bio: Presiding Judge of the 48th District Court since a 2021 appointment; formerly an attorney in the Civil Division of the Tarrant County District Attorney's Office.

positions.stance: Believes in "applying the law as written and honoring the Constitution," delivering "fair, impartial rulings rooted in the law, not politics."

tx-tarrant-2026-coa2-p7-walker-brian.name: Brian Walker
tx-tarrant-2026-coa2-p7-walker-brian.bio: Justice on the Second Court of Appeals; former Air Force Reserve judge advocate (JAG) and former criminal prosecutor.

tx-tarrant-2026-dj213-ferry-michael.name: Michael Ferry
tx-tarrant-2026-dj213-ferry-michael.bio: Judge of the 213th District Court since a 2026 appointment; former Tarrant County assistant district attorney, retired DEA special agent and former U.S. Navy officer.

positions.stance: Believes "Judges must apply the law as written - not legislate from the bench."

tx-tarrant-2026-dj236-fillmore-dusty.name: Dusty Fillmore
tx-tarrant-2026-dj236-fillmore-dusty.bio: Lawyer for more than three decades whose practice at The Fillmore Law Firm centered on complex civil trials and appeals.

tx-tarrant-2026-dj297-allin-amy.name: Amy Allin
tx-tarrant-2026-dj297-allin-amy.bio: Judge of the 297th District Court since April 2025; former prosecutor with the Tarrant County District Attorney's Office.

tx-tarrant-2026-dj297-howey-fred.name: Fred Howey
tx-tarrant-2026-dj297-howey-fred.bio: Felony criminal defense attorney at Dunham & Jones and U.S. Army Reserve veteran.

positions.stance: "My judicial philosophy is that the Judge makes rulings based on the laws as written and should never legislate from the bench."

tx-tarrant-2026-dj372-lugo-julie.name: Julie Lugo
tx-tarrant-2026-dj372-lugo-julie.bio: Judge of the 372nd District Court since 2022; former Tarrant County assistant criminal district attorney.

tx-tarrant-2026-dj432-sorrells-lee.name: Lee Sorrells
tx-tarrant-2026-dj432-sorrells-lee.bio: Associate Judge of the 323rd District Court since 2024; former Tarrant County prosecutor and sheriff's deputy.

tx-tarrant-2026-dj432-miller-courtney.name: Courtney Miller
tx-tarrant-2026-dj432-miller-courtney.bio: Criminal defense attorney since 2008 and former prosecutor.

tx-tarrant-2026-dj485-jumes-steven.name: Steven Jumes
tx-tarrant-2026-dj485-jumes-steven.bio: Felony district judge since 2022; former prosecutor with the U.S. Attorney's Office and the Tarrant County District Attorney's Office.

positions.stance: Pledges: "I will follow the law as written," "I will never legislate from the bench," and "I will always protect and defend the Constitution."

tx-tarrant-2026-cdj1-wagner-sherri.name: Sherri Wagner
tx-tarrant-2026-cdj1-wagner-sherri.bio: Associate Judge of the 323rd District Court since 2023; former criminal prosecutor for over 20 years.

tx-tarrant-2026-cdj1-stormer-cindy.name: Cindy Stormer
tx-tarrant-2026-cdj1-stormer-cindy.bio: Former police officer, elected Cooke County district attorney, chief of a Dallas DA mental health division, and retired professor.

tx-tarrant-2026-cdj3-allen-douglas.name: Douglas Allen
tx-tarrant-2026-cdj3-allen-douglas.bio: Judge of Criminal District Court No. 3 since a 2023 appointment; former Assistant U.S. Attorney and Tarrant County assistant district attorney.

tx-tarrant-2026-cdj4-porter-andy.name: Andy Porter
tx-tarrant-2026-cdj4-porter-andy.bio: Judge of Criminal District Court No. 4 since 2023; former Tarrant County assistant criminal district attorney.

positions.stance: Believes "legislatures write laws, not judges," noting judges have "the most limited role in government" by constitutional design.
"A textualist at heart," believes statutes "should be narrowly construed to effect the Texas Legislature's expressed purpose" in compliance with federal and state constitutions.
Believes judges "should show respect for the law, the litigants, and the litigators who appear in court."
Believes "the public deserves an efficient judicial system."

tx-tarrant-2026-fdj231-barrows-leslie.name: Leslie Barrows
tx-tarrant-2026-fdj231-barrows-leslie.bio: Family law attorney and licensed mediator who founded the Barrows Firm.

tx-tarrant-2026-fdj231-newell-lyndsay.name: Lyndsay Newell
tx-tarrant-2026-fdj231-newell-lyndsay.bio: Partner at a Fort Worth law firm and former teacher.

tx-tarrant-2026-fdj322-munford-james.name: James B. Munford
tx-tarrant-2026-fdj322-munford-james.bio: Judge of the 322nd District Court since 2018; former associate judge of that court for 11 years and board-certified family law attorney.

tx-tarrant-2026-fdj323-kim-alex.name: Alex Kim
tx-tarrant-2026-fdj323-kim-alex.bio: Judge of the 323rd District Court since 2019.

positions.stance: His judicial philosophy "is guided by the timeless principles of the Constitution"; as "a devoted originalist," believes "judges must apply the law as written — not legislate from the bench."
Will "interpret statutes and the Constitution faithfully — no more, no less — without legislating from the bench."

tx-tarrant-2026-fdj324-gayden-crystal.name: Crystal Gayden
tx-tarrant-2026-fdj324-gayden-crystal.bio: Attorney who built her own law firm representing families across Tarrant County.
